source.title: Transformers Discover Molecular Structure Without Graph Priors
source.authors: T. Kreiman; Yu-Tong Bai; Fadi Atieh; Elizabeth Weaver; Eric Qu; Aditi S. Krishnapriyan

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present and not cut off. There are minor equation and layout extraction artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law experiments to molecular energy and force modeling with Transformers, a different domain from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper tests analogous scaling behavior in molecular modeling, not held-out language-model cross-entropy. Scaling-law results cited from other work are not this study's results. The synthetic-data experiment on attention exponents and the other physical-structure analyses do not measure the loss scaling or allocation behavior in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study fits and checks power-law scaling of validation loss with model size and epochs for Transformers trained on molecular energy/force data (OMol25), in both autoregressive pre-training and fine-tuning. That is a result on whether the power-law form holds outside text pretraining (V5). The models are not language models, so V1–V4 and V6–V7, which concern language-model loss, allocation and fitting, are not directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that molecular Transformers scale predictably with training resources in pre-training and fine-tuning, consistent with Hoffmann et al. They report that fine-tuning fits from 5M–90M models predict the 306M model, that IsoFLOP curves are parabolic with power-law optimal size, and that pre-training loss shows no saturation at 1B. They speculate that gains may continue to hundreds of billions of parameters.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a graph-free Transformer on molecular structures and evaluates molecular prediction performance, rather than measuring language-model held-out cross-entropy or the original language-model scaling setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports separate pre-training and fine-tuning scaling experiments, with different training objectives and schedules; it does not report a comparison of fitted scaling results across alternative fitting methods.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic pairwise-potential data, the attention-derived interaction exponent approaches the true exponent as data and model size grow (R²=0.98 correlation).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned internal structure (attention decay exponent) converges toward the true physical form with scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Log-probability correlation with other models' force errors is stronger at 1B than 163M parameters (SPICE).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uncertainty-quantification quality of generative Transformers improves with model size.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is presented mainly in figures without numerical fitted exponents or uncertainty estimates. The reported extrapolation is limited to the 306M fine-tuned model, and the pre-training sweep reports a power-law trend but not an out-of-fit prediction.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the claim versions were omitted. The synthetic-data attention-exponent experiment and the water-dimer, molecular-dynamics, and other physical-structure results do not measure the scaling outcomes named in these versions.

untested.parts: No language-model loss is measured; scaling is shown for molecular Transformers only.
No language-model extrapolation. The molecular extrapolation (90M to 306M) spans less than one order of magnitude.
No language-model allocation. Optimal token/data count versus compute and the parameter-vs-data exponent comparison are not reported, even for the molecular models.
Shape at fixed parameter count is not varied.
Only the molecular domain is tested; data-size scaling and fitted exponents are not reported. Epoch scaling implicitly involves repeated data but is not analysed as such.
Downstream predictability is not tested as a scaling relation.
No comparison of fitting choices or setups, and no curvature analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 and V3 links were moved to V5 because the systems are molecular, not language, models. The 1B-vs-eSEN comparison (Table I) is the study's own method against a baseline, not a scaling result, so no row is needed. None of the reported rows gives numeric exponents or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The models are molecular Transformers, not language models, and the reported scaling results are molecular prediction performance rather than held-out language-model pretraining loss.
The reported extrapolation is to a 306M-parameter molecular model; extrapolation across several orders of magnitude is not demonstrated.
The study reports an optimal model-size trend across compute budgets, but does not report how optimal token count grows with compute or compare parameter and token growth exponents.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
The tested domain is molecular modeling. Other modalities, repeated-data regimes, and transfer settings are not tested.
The study does not test whether downstream-task performance improves predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
The study does not compare fitting choices or setups to determine whether exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on them, nor does it report curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: Transformer (OMol25 4M fine-tuning scaling sweep)
rows.operation_detail: Fit power-law performance curves from smaller model sizes and training epochs, then evaluate the larger model.

conditions.value: identical across runs except parameter count and training epochs

rows.measure: Validation loss/performance as a function of model size and training epochs
rows.locator: Neural Scaling Analysis, Fig. 2a; fine-tuning scaling laws
rows.note: The authors state that power-law curves fitted using the three smaller models accurately predict the performance of the 306M model. The plotted numerical values are not available in the text.
rows.check: Molecular Transformers, not language models, so the row bears on V5 rather than V2. Extrapolation is only about 3.4x (90M to 306M), not orders of magnitude. The fit uses model size and epochs (repeated passes over the same 4M data). The measure is fine-tuning validation loss (energy+force MAE). Main text points to Fig. 2b for the 306M prediction, while the caption puts it in 2a. Figure only, no fitted exponents.

rows.subject: Transformer (OMol25 4M fine-tuning IsoFLOP sweep)
rows.operation_detail: Construct predicted IsoFLOP curves and identify the optimal model size and achievable performance at fixed training compute.

conditions.value: constant training compute per IsoFLOP curve
varied; smaller models trained longer and larger models for fewer epochs

rows.measure: Predicted validation performance and optimal model size at fixed compute
rows.locator: Neural Scaling Analysis, Fig. 2b; fine-tuning scaling laws
rows.note: The authors describe the predicted IsoFLOP curves as parabolic and the optimal model size and achievable performance as following consistent power-law relationships. Numerical curve values are not available in the text.
rows.check: Molecular domain, so V5 only, not V3. The IsoFLOP curves are predicted from the fitted law, not measured runs, so the optimal-size power law partly follows from the assumed functional form. Token/data growth with compute is not reported. Figure only.

rows.subject: Transformer (OMol25 4M pre-training scaling sweep)
rows.size_stated: Seven model sizes, up to 1B parameters
rows.operation_detail: Train models of varying sizes with other training hyperparameters fixed and assess evaluation performance against model size.
rows.measure: Evaluation performance as a function of model size
rows.locator: Appendix C.3, Fig. 17; Pre-training Scaling Laws
rows.note: The authors describe a clear power-law relationship with model size and report no sign of saturation up to 1B parameters. Numerical curve values are not available in the text.
rows.check: The measure is pre-training validation loss (cross-entropy over discretized molecular tokens) versus non-embedding parameters for seven sizes up to about 1.2B (Table III: 800k–1.2B), 10 epochs. No out-of-fit prediction, no exponent and no uncertainty are reported. Figure only.

relationships.condition: Graph-free LLaMA2-style Transformers on OMol25 4M molecular energy/force data, in pre-training (to ~1B params) and fine-tuning (5M–306M)
relationships.reason: Authors report clear power-law loss scaling with size and epochs and accurate prediction of the held-out 306M model (R1, R2, R3). The evidence is figures only, with no exponents.
relationships.display_finding: Reported power laws in model size and epochs accurately predict the held-out 306M model, although exponents are unreported.
